output.problem: The country faces frequent and more complex natural hazards, while disaster risk reduction, climate adaptation and disaster response are spread across several bodies. The bill proposes one department to lead disaster and climate resilience, from risk reduction to recovery.
output.problem_quote: Every year, Filipino communities face the devastating impact of typhoons, floods, earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and other natural hazards.

rows.section_ref: Section 4 (Creation of the Department of Disaster Resilience)
rows.target_quote: There is hereby created the Department of Disaster Resilience, hereinafter referred to as the Department.

comparator.quote: The mandate of the Department shall cover all natural hazards, including the effects of climate change, such as the following:
comparator.title: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF DISASTER RESILIENCE, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

rows.differences: HB No. 4652 has a separate mandate section that lists the natural hazards the Department covers (geological, hydrological and meteorological, and the effects of climate change); this bill states the mandate in general terms within the creation section.
rows.why: Listing the hazards covered would mark where the Department's functions end and those kept by the DND, the OCD and the DSWD for human-induced disasters begin.
rows.tradeoffs: A defined list gives clarity but may need amendment as new hazards are recognized.

rows.target_quote: The Secretary shall possess substantial experience and demonstrated competence in disaster risk reduction and management

comparator.quote: The Secretary shall preferably have a solid background in any
comparator.title: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF DISASTER RESILIENCE, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

rows.differences: SB No. 173 states the Secretary's background only as a preference; this bill requires substantial experience and demonstrated competence in the field.
rows.why: A stated qualification standard supports a competent head for a technical department.
rows.tradeoffs: Stricter qualifications narrow the pool of appointees.

rows.target_quote: Accordingly, the CCC and NDRRMC are hereby abolished.
rows.differences: The related bills carry the same transfer of functions; none offers a different arrangement.
rows.why: Abolishing the CCC and the NDRRMC and transferring their functions avoids keeping parallel bodies.
rows.tradeoffs: Splitting disaster functions by type of hazard leaves the OCD and the DND with human-induced disasters, which needs clear coordination rules.
rows.gap: How the OCD's remaining functions and personnel are divided between the OCD and the Department is not stated.

rows.section_ref: Section 70 (Appropriations and Management of Disaster Resilience Fund)
rows.target_quote: The budget of the Department shall be composed of the following, which shall be collectively called the Disaster Resilience Fund:
rows.differences: The related bills carry the same Disaster Resilience Fund and appropriations clause; none offers a different funding design.
rows.why: No related measure offers a better alternative; the funding design is reviewed in ApprAIsal.
rows.tradeoffs: Lump-sum and continuing funds give flexibility in emergencies but reduce the detail of budget authorization.

rows.target_quote: All laws, decrees, executive orders, rules and regulations inconsistent with this Act are hereby repealed or modified accordingly.

comparator.quote: The provisions of Republic Act no. 10121, Republic Act no. 7160, Republic Act no. 7916, Republic Act no. 9184
comparator.title: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF DISASTER RESILIENCE, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

rows.differences: SB No. 173 names the laws it amends or repeals (RA Nos. 10121, 7160, 7916 and 9184); this bill uses a general repealing clause although it abolishes bodies created by law.
rows.why: Naming the laws affected avoids doubt on which provisions on the NDRRMC, the CCC and procurement remain in force.
rows.tradeoffs: A specific list must be complete, or provisions left out may be read as still in force.
rows.gap: Whether RA No. 9729, which created the CCC, should also be named could not be established from the material.

duplications.existing: Office of Civil Defense and the Department of National Defense, which keep functions on human-induced disasters
duplications.note: Natural-disaster functions move to the Department while the OCD, the DND and other agencies keep human-induced disaster functions, so two systems for disaster preparedness and response would coexist.
duplications.quote: shall continue to perform their functions related to the management of human- induced disasters

cost_notes.why: At least four undersecretaries, with no upper limit.
A regional office in each administrative region, headed by a Regional Director.
A national operations center, alternative command centers and a research and training institute, within one year.
Magna Carta benefits and, under Section 91 (Hazard Pay), hazard pay for all personnel add to Personnel Services.
Funds, positions and assets of the absorbed bodies are transferred, offsetting part of the new requirement.

cost_notes.item: Section 92 (Separation Benefits of Officials and Employees of Affected Agencies)
cost_notes.why: A separation plan of one and one-half months' salary for every year of service for displaced employees.

memo_part.heading: On the mandate of the Department
paragraphs: 4.1 Section 4 of HB No. 9897 creates the Department as the principal government institution for disaster and climate resilience, while Section 81 leaves the management of human-induced disasters with the DND, the DILG, the DSWD and the OCD. It may be noted that the bill does not state which hazards fall within the Department's mandate. In this regard, may we recommend that the natural hazards covered by the Department be specified, similar to Section 5 of HB No. 4652, so that its functions are clearly delineated from those that remain with the existing agencies.

memo_part.heading: On the repealing clause
paragraphs: 4.2 Section 99 provides a general repealing clause, although the bill abolishes the Climate Change Commission and the NDRRMC and sets exceptions to the procurement law. May we recommend that the laws amended or repealed be expressly identified, similar to Section 100 of SB No. 173, which names RA Nos. 10121, 7160, 7916 and 9184, to avoid doubt on the provisions that remain in force.

reviewer_checks: Confirm how the OCD's functions and personnel would be divided between the OCD and the Department under Section 81.
Check whether RA No. 9729 should also be named among the laws amended or repealed.
Note that HB Nos. 6371, 4652 and 2384 and SB No. 173 carry largely the same provisions, so few design alternatives are available.

self_critique.objection: A fixed list of hazards may leave out compound or new hazards that fall between natural and human-induced disasters, such as a typhoon followed by a fire in an evacuation center.
self_critique.condition: The list is illustrative and paired with a rule on which agency leads when hazards combine.

self_critique.objection: Qualification requirements in law narrow the pool for a cabinet post, while SB No. 173 leaves them as a preference.
Splitting functions by type of hazard keeps the OCD and the DND for human-induced disasters, so the reform may create a second response system instead of consolidating one.
self_critique.condition: The bill delineates the OCD's remaining functions and the transfer of its personnel, as raised in Part VI.

self_critique.objection: Retaining lump-sum contingency funds and continuing appropriations because no related bill differs is not itself a reason; they reduce budget detail and accountability.
self_critique.condition: The amounts and release rules are set in the annual GAA, as reviewed in ApprAIsal's Part V.

self_critique.objection: A specific list can omit laws: SB No. 173's list does not name RA No. 9729, which created the Climate Change Commission that this bill abolishes.
self_critique.condition: The list includes RA No. 9729 and a general clause remains for other inconsistent laws.

theory_of_change.problem: Disaster risk reduction, climate adaptation and disaster response are spread across several bodies
theory_of_change.mechanism: One department absorbs the CCC, the NDRRMC and the natural-disaster functions of the OCD and the DSWD, with regional and local offices and a Disaster Resilience Fund
theory_of_change.outcome: Faster, coordinated preparedness and response, and fewer losses from natural hazards
theory_of_change.weakest_assumption: That separating natural from human-induced disasters still leaves a clear line of command in mixed events
